market_context: United States/Canada; household dishwasher troubleshooting focused on filters, drain hose, sink plumbing, air gaps and disposal connections.
title: Why Won't My Dishwasher Drain? Common Causes and Fixes

seo.title: Dishwasher Not Draining? What to Check Step by Step
seo.meta_description: Check whether the water is truly excessive, clean the filter, inspect the hose, sink drain, air gap and disposal connection. Learn when the drain pump needs service.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose standing water in a dishwasher, resolve common filter, plumbing and installation restrictions, and distinguish them from a drain-pump or control failure.

excerpt: If a large amount of water remains in the dishwasher, remove visible debris and clean the user-accessible filters first, make sure the kitchen sink drains normally, and check the dishwasher hose for kinks or blockages. If your setup has an air gap or garbage disposal, inspect that connection too. Do not put chemical drain cleaner in the dishwasher; persistent failure may need service.
content_html:
You open the dishwasher and find water in the bottom. Before deciding the drain pump has failed, ask a more basic question: is this actually too much water, or is it the small amount some models normally keep in the sump area?

Dishwashers are not all designed the same way. GE notes that on some models, water in the filter or sump area can be normal as long as it does not cover the bottom of the tub. The problem is more convincing when the water clearly covers the base, smells stale, remains after a completed drain cycle or appears with a drain error.

Start with a simple test: cancel and drain

Use the manual to activate Cancel/Drain or the equivalent function for your model. Close the door fully and listen.

If you hear the pump and the level drops, the original cycle may simply have been interrupted. If the pump runs but little water moves, a restriction is more likely. If there is no drain attempt at all, the issue may involve the pump, controls, sensor or door-latch system.

Before removing serviceable parts, disconnect power as the manual directs.

Clear the large debris you can safely reach

A food label, bone, noodle, piece of glass or other object can cover the sump area or interfere with the filter.

Pull out the lower rack and inspect the floor in good light. Remove only debris you can safely reach. If broken glass is present, use protective gloves and do not reach blindly into openings.

Do not remove pump covers unless your model's manual identifies them as owner-serviceable.

The filter is one of the highest-value checks

Many current dishwashers have a removable filter assembly in the bottom. Take it out according to the manual, remove debris and rinse it. A soft brush can help with greasy buildup without damaging the mesh.

Lock the filter back into place correctly. A loose or misinstalled filter can hurt wash performance and allow debris to circulate.

If your dishwasher does not have an obvious removable filter, do not force parts because a different brand's video showed one.

Then look at the sink: the two systems often share a drain

The dishwasher usually empties into plumbing under the kitchen sink. If the sink itself drains slowly, gurgles or backs up, the restriction may be in the household plumbing rather than inside the appliance.

Address the sink or branch-drain problem first. GE specifically advises against using drain cleaner in the dishwasher.

If you have a garbage disposal, make sure the drain path at that connection is clear and follow the disposal's instructions. Never put your hand into a disposal to check for an obstruction.

A newly installed disposal has one very specific clue

The dishwasher inlet on a new garbage disposal is normally closed by an internal knockout plug. If the dishwasher hose is connected before that plug is removed, there is nowhere for the dishwasher water to go.

GE lists this as a common reason a dishwasher suddenly stops draining after a disposal replacement.

If you are unsure how the connection was made, check the disposal installation instructions or have the installer verify it.

Inspect the drain hose without turning this into a plumbing remodel

The dishwasher drain hose can kink behind the machine or clog where it connects under the sink.

Inspect the accessible section for sharp bends or crushing. If you need to pull the dishwasher from the cabinet to reach the rest, check the manual first and shut off power and water as appropriate.

An old reused hose can deform or accumulate debris. If the dishwasher manufacturer specifies a particular hose or routing, follow that setup.

The air gap can become the bottleneck

Some installations use a small air-gap fitting on the sink or countertop. Its job is to keep contaminated sink water from flowing backward toward the dishwasher.

If you have one, remove its cap as the maintenance instructions allow and clean visible debris. A clogged air gap can cause poor draining or water discharge from the fitting.

If your installation does not use an air gap, you do not need to add one merely as a troubleshooting step; the correct setup depends on local code and the appliance installation instructions.

Drain-hose height is part of the system too

Where an air gap is not used, many installations require a high loop in the dishwasher drain hose, secured under the countertop before the hose connects to the sink drain or disposal.

GE notes that the loop height must match the installation requirements. A hose that has fallen or is routed incorrectly can contribute to drainage or backflow problems.

Too many suds can confuse the diagnosis

Hand dishwashing liquid or excessive detergent can create heavy suds. GE notes that oversudsing can interfere with draining and may also cause leaks.

Use only detergent intended for automatic dishwashers and dose it appropriately for the product, load and water hardness.

When the drain pump becomes more likely

If the filter and visible sump area are clear, the sink drains normally, the hose and connections are open and the installation is correct, the drain pump or its control may need diagnosis.

A hum with no water movement can point to a jammed or failed pump. Silence when the control is commanding a drain can involve the pump, wiring or control system. Confirming those faults generally requires access and measurements.

Do not bypass the door switch or apply power directly to components as a test.

Run one test and watch where the water goes

After cleaning a filter or correcting a hose, reassemble everything and run a short cycle or drain function.

Watch under the sink for leakage at any connection you touched and inspect the dishwasher floor when the cycle finishes. If only the small sump level described as normal for your model remains, there is no reason to chase a perfectly bone-dry tub.

The useful sequence is tub and filter, sink drain, connection, hose, installation, and only then the pump. Following the water path keeps you from dismantling the dishwasher when the restriction was a few inches away under the sink.

faq.question: Is it normal to have a little water in the bottom of the dishwasher?
faq.answer: On some models, yes, particularly in the sump or filter area. Check the manual; water that clearly covers the tub floor is more likely to indicate a drain problem.

faq.question: Can I put drain cleaner in my dishwasher?
faq.answer: No. GE advises against using drain-cleaning chemicals inside the dishwasher.

faq.question: Why did my dishwasher stop draining after a new garbage disposal was installed?
faq.answer: A common cause is that the disposal's dishwasher-inlet knockout plug was not removed before the drain hose was connected.

faq.question: When is the drain pump likely to need service?
faq.answer: If the filter, hose, sink drain and connections are clear but the dishwasher still cannot evacuate water, the pump or control system may need professional diagnosis.
